newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down, under support.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply down, under support.

text.p: CSCE March world sugar futures continued to rack-up losses after midday and closed on the lows after taking out support at 10.35 cents a lb.
March ended down 0.12 to 10.35, having ranged from 10.46 to 10.33. The back months finished 0.05 lower to 0.01 higher.
Subsequent major support was pegged at 10.20, a year low basis the March contract, dealers said.
They cited steady speculative selling and light trade buying throughout the session.
Volume was estimated at a moderate 16,762 lots.
Market sources blamed ongoing losses on the global supply and demand balance.
"Last year, a good part (of the surplus) was in India so the sugar was not readily available to the market," said Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes.
She noted strong offtake a year ago in Poland, Turkey and the Phillippines but "this year, they all have better crops and will not be taking sugar off the world market."
Wednesday, F.O. Licht put the 1995/96 surplus at 8 million tonnes.
